Subject: Renewal structure: hybrid-duration alignment and staircase burst pool

Hi Nikhil,

Our renewal for Crestline AI is coming up in mid-November and we're trying to consolidate a plan that addresses both predictable committed capacity and the occasional high-throughput events we run (model retrains, end-of-quarter traffic spikes).

Key asks from my side:
- Can Redwood support a multi-year arrangement where Year 1 has a softer commit (to match our initial scale) and Year 2+ ramp faster (staircase style)?
- We need a small shared "burst pool" we can draw from for short windows (up to 72 hours) without over-provisioning dedicated capacity.
- Want clarity on auto-renew behavior and opt-out notice windows.

I've attached our Q3 usage snapshot to help ground numbers. Would appreciate a sketch of terms (duration, ramp schedule, burst pool sizing and pricing bands) we could discuss next week.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director of Cloud Ops
Crestline AI

Attachment: crestline_usage_report_q3.csv (CSV, 120KB)

Subject: Re: Renewal structure: hybrid-duration alignment and staircase burst pool

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage file. Happy to put together a proposal. High-level thoughts below so the call is productive:

1) Hybrid-duration structure
- Option A: 2-year term with a 12-month soft-commit (lower guaranteed units) then a firm increase in Year 2 (staircase). We can also do a frontloaded credit to smooth impact in Year 1.
- Option B: 3-year front-loaded annualization (more predictable pricing) with an option to accelerate Year 2 commit if you cross X% of baseline.

2) Burst pool
- We can provision a shared burst pool (reserve of units billed at a higher short-term rate) that auto-fills up to a cap and drains based on usage. Short windows (<=72h) will be accommodated without spinning new dedicated capacity.
- We can size the pool as a % of average daily peak; propose a working draft for your Q3 peaks.

3) Auto-renew & notifications
- Standard opt-in auto-renew with a 60-day notice window by default; we can negotiate 30-day window for enterprise customers.

Next steps: I'll attach a pricing sketch for a staircase ramp (spreadsheet) and let Monica/Marissa take a look for finance/legal implications. Can we schedule 30m on Tue or Wed next week to review?

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Nikhil — Tue 10/13 at 11am PT works for us. Couple of clarifications we'd like included in the sketch:
- Year 1 ramp: can we compress the ramp so committed units hit 70% of projected production by month 6 (instead of month 9)? That helps our launch timeline.
- Burst pool sizing: we'd prefer a burst cap that can cover ~25% of our largest peak day for up to 48 hours. If that's too expensive, give incremental bands so we can choose.
- Credits: if we prepay some portion, can you give a modest discount on burst rates?

Appreciate the draft and see you Tue.

Best,
Samantha

All — good plan. I reviewed the numbers Nikhil attached and ran preliminary finance checks. We can accommodate:
- compressed 6-month ramp in Year 1 (assumes Crestline keeps monthly usage reporting and meets the 70% threshold or billing auto-adjusts)
- a configurable burst pool with tiered pricing (Base / +25% / +50%) — we'll price burst tiers at a premium to committed units but allow a -10% delta if customer prepays >=25% of Year 1 committed value.
- auto-renew: we should keep default 60-day opt-out for standard contracts for headroom on forecasting, but can make a 30-day notice as a one-off for Crestline if deals desk signs off.

Markus, please draft the amendment language: include a "Burst Pool Addendum" (defines measurement windows, cap, and overage bands), a short ramp schedule table, and the opt-out notice clause. Marissa, please prepare the pricing worksheet we can send to the customer after the call.

I'll coordinate with legal to have a draft ready within 5 business days. Nikhil — confirm call notes and send us any follow-up clarifications from the meeting.
